- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots and continues upward; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast slope by 10–15% in next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >75% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to be flat; introduce slight upward bias if price is trending down, or downward if trending up.
